parsed.explanation: Combined regime: no state bathroom ban or presentation offence and local ordinances cover the largest city and ~30% of population, but federal entry screening can refuse on sex discrepancy and pursue permanent fraud ineligibility, federal facilities exclude congruent access, federal/immigration custody documents hormone removal, forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse, and the state provides no statewide public-accommodations or hate-crime coverage. National threat-framing of 'radically pro-transgender' groups and unresolved litigation leave remedies partial. This is unremedied universal federal exposure plus severe custody risk, softened only locally.

entry_documents.exposure: X-marker national passports stopped Feb 2025; entry cable directs refusal where documents/records discrepancy or reasonable doubt on sex, and permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility consideration for wilful misrepresentation. Passports confiscated/blocked, travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration. Civil-liberties suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs is pending and Supreme Court action allowed restrictions to take effect; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from refusal to fraud finding, detention, and birth-sex custody/care exposures; state facility openness does not cancel federal entry screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026 adopted conversion-therapy model: short haircuts, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; care denial reported and trans-prisoner reporting stopped. Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse reported for trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders have been blocked/enjoined; national hate-crime statute provides theoretical recourse. No documented remedy changing custody practices.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry fraud allegation or facility trespass in other jurisdictions can move traveller into federal/state custody where documented abuse and care denial apply; state ban on public funds for prison transition care adds exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. State itself has no bathroom ban; 2016 birth-certificate law repealed 30 Mar 2017, no facility-use crime, but 2025 revival bill leaves position open.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No state statute bars facility matching gender identity. Largest city and one county ordinances explicitly cover gender identity from 1 Jan 2022; ~30% population under local ordinance.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection does not cancel federal facilities ban; traveller must navigate two sovereigns, with federal exposure in federal buildings and state/local openness elsewhere.

care_services.exposure: State laws effective 2023 end puberty blockers, hormone therapy and surgery under 18; 2025 law bars state funds for minor and prisoner transition care. National orders target minor gender-affirming care and proposed rules would bar public insurance under 18.
care_services.protection: Not documented. No operative traveller-facing care protection is documented in dossier.
care_services.interaction: Minor traveller or detained adult encounters care denial; emergency/adult visitor care access is not documented as restricted, but custody care is withdrawn.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Jan 2025 order redefines sex binary for national purposes; 2025-26 DOJ reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology' and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups. Orders direct investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders blocked/enjoined and passport policy remains challenged.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing increases probability officials treat discrepancy/presentation as fraud or extremism, raising entry, school and custody exposure for adults and minors.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bars AMAB from female sports/athletic teams, including visiting trans athletes; parents'-rights law requires notification if student requests different name/pronoun; minor transition care banned and publicly unfunded.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No visitor-minor safeguard, guardian recognition protocol, or care-access shield is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling family with minor faces sports exclusion, school-notification risk if enrolled, and care denial; national teacher-prosecution order creates guardian/educator exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime statute covers neither gender identity nor sexual orientation, so bias assault may not be charged as bias crime under state law. Violence rate comparison is not established; 3.0 per 100k figure is acknowledged undercount and is not used per rubric.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate crimes punishable nationally; only 23 states cover GI in state bias statutes per dossier. Local ordinances in some areas may help but coverage is patchy.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of state bias coverage plus federal threat-framing weakens police response; local ordinance areas provide partial, geographically uneven recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide private employment, housing or public-accommodations protection; answer depends on city/county. 2025 bathroom bill text/coverage and local facility enforcement not established; amended-certificate display effect on licences not established.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National litigation, enjoined orders, national hate-crime statute and local ordinances exist, but no documented remedy has reversed federal passport, facility or custody policies.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved federal litigation means exposure depends on measures in effect at travel; unknown state bill could add facility ban on top of federal regime.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-1 custody/facility exposure with complaints not altering practice, but here state has no bathroom ban and local ordinances exist, while federal custody abuse is documented nationally. Slightly less universal than 0.35-B's hospital/detention placement, yet entry fraud risk is added.

Similar to 0.45-A's unremedied government-building bathroom exclusion with polite public and no presentation offence, but scope is federal-only plus entry discrepancy/fraud, while state facilities are open. That narrower facility scope offsets the more severe entry consequence, leaving rating near 0.45.

Lower than 0.55-E, where border humiliation was partially disciplined and a tribunal secured compensation, with no mandatory birth-sex rule. Here discrepancy can cause refusal/permanent ineligibility, remedies are unresolved litigation, and custody harm is more severe.

parsed.synthesis: State layer is comparatively open on facilities and has local ordinances, but combined regime is governed by federal entry, facilities and custody exposures that state law cannot cancel. Passport discrepancy, permanent fraud risk, federal facility exclusion, hormone-removal custody, immigration-custody abuse, minor care/sports bans and absent statewide accommodations/hate-crime protection produce recurring institutional exposure without demonstrated effective remedy. Local openness and litigation are partial mitigations, not overrides, placing the case in elevated risk near the 0.45 anchor.
